readout_other: verbal report of nociceptive response (thumb); UV-Vis spectrophotometry of propofol released from nanoparticles
direction_notes: Ultrasound through the skull with RTT correction evoked nociceptive responses in the thumb (62.7% response rate) and released propofol from nanoparticles; neither occurred without correction.
safety_notes: No detrimental effects were reported by the subjects during or following the stimulation.

exposures.label: Nerve stimulation of the human thumb through an ex-vivo skull

target.label: peripheral nerves within the human thumb

device.model: two spherically focused 126-element arrays driven by Vantage256 (Verasonics)

timing.protocol_description: A single 300 ms stimulus delivered every 8-12 s in randomised order, 10 repetitions of each of eight stimulus types (correction method x pressure level, plus sham) per subject, 80 trials per subject.

exposures.label: Propofol release from nanoparticles in vials inside an ex-vivo skull

target.label: vials of nanoparticle solution at a central location within the skull

device.model: two spherically focused 126-element arrays driven by Vantage256 (Verasonics)

timing.protocol_description: The ultrasound was pulsed for 100 ms every 1 s for 60 s; n = 10 vials per condition, conditions randomly interleaved.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Specifically, we instructed 11 human subjects to place their thumb into a holder at the central target inside an ex-vivo skull.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The arrays delivered into the target a 300 ms stimulus at a frequency of 650 kHz
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: The LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH labels correspond to an intended peak pressure of 1.3, 1.55, and 1.8 MPa, as measured in free-field.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The ultrasound stimuli were 300 ms in duration.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: The transducers were driven by a programmable system (Vantage256, Verasonics) with an external power supply (QPX600DP, Aim and Thurlby Thandar Instruments).
source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound, delivered through the skull, impacted the nanoparticles in 100 ms pulses delivered every 1 s for 60 s, at a frequency of 650 kHz and pressure amplitude of 1.8 MPa.
source_quotes.exposures[1].free_field.pressure_kpa: For hydrophone- and RTT-corrected stimuli, we varied the intended peak pressure levels across 1.3, 1.55, and 1.8 MPa.
source_quotes.exposures[1].timing.pulse_duration_ms: The ultrasound was pulsed for 100 ms every 1 s for 60 s to align with previous studies (Airan et al., 2017; Wilson et al., 2024).

source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: The results shown in Figure 3A were only at the highest pressure level: 1.8 MPa in free-field, 1.84 MPa with hydrophone correction, 0.73 MPa with no correction, and 1.95 MPa with the RTT correction.
source_quotes.exposures[1].in_situ.pressure_kpa: The results shown in Figure 2A were only at the highest pressure level: 1.8 MPa in free-field, 1.84 MPa with hydrophone correction, 0.73 MPa with no correction, and 1.95 MPa with the RTT correction.

flags.reason: Intended peak pressure levels 1.3, 1.55 and 1.8 MPa (nerve) and 1.2, 1.5 and 1.8 MPa (drug release) were swept; only the highest, 1.8 MPa in free-field, is recorded. Pressures with skull and correction (0.73, 1.84, 1.95 MPa) not placed in any domain.
Sweep of 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 MPa; only 1.8 MPa recorded.
Duty cycle not stated; 100 ms every 1 s not converted.
Array device is described as previously published; maker not named; Verasonics is driving electronics only.
Only one ex-vivo skull; nerve stimulation was in living human thumbs placed inside the skull; drug release used vials of nanoparticle solution.
A blinded experimenter recorded percepts; subjects' blinding to condition inferred from earmuffs and closed eyes, not stated as single-blind.
Sham steered the focus 10 mm below the target; a no-ultrasound vial control was also used for drug release.
